name: bluewater-tales-93-102
lines: This is the oldest customer complaint in the world.
It is three thousand seven hundred years old. And it is furious.
The city of Ur. Around seventeen fifty BC.
A man named Nanni pays a merchant for fine copper.
The merchant is Ea-nasir. The copper shows up. It's junk.
So Nanni sends a servant to get his money back.
Ea-nasir sends him home with nothing. More than once.
So Nanni does what angry customers do. He writes a review.
Except there is no phone. He presses every word into wet clay. Front and back.
He writes that he has been treated with contempt. And he wants his money back, in full.
And here's the best part. Ea-nasir kept it.
Archaeologists found it in his house. With more complaints, from more customers.
Today it belongs to the British Museum. And the whole internet knows his name.
Not for his copper. For one unhappy customer.
A complaint used to take clay and a long walk. Now it takes ten seconds.
So fix it while it's still a conversation. Before it becomes a record.
